view: This is a first public print for a data-center white-space infrastructure maker: power distribution, RPPs/PDUs and the SkyBridge modular platform. Customers are concentrated (two took 61.2% of direct revenue in 2025). The stock has broken its issue price, and almost all of the break came with the sector, not with company news. The arithmetic of consensus looks conservative. H1-26 revenue was $437.5M, against $289M in H2-25 and $158.6M in H1-25. Backlog went from $419M at year-end 2025 to $1.11B in June 2026, and Q2 book-to-bill was 3.5x. Yet FY26 consensus of $902M implies H2-26 of only about $464M, just 6% above H1. The range across four analysts is about $6M wide, which looks like numbers walked from management's IPO model, not independent estimates. A revenue beat and a FY26 raise are therefore more likely than not. The demand backdrop since the IPO also helps. Vertiv's Q3 on 10-28 had organic orders more than double and raised its 2026 sales guide by about $650M. Hyperscalers raised 2026 capex in late-October calls and pointed to more in 2027. The offsets are what keep this from a call. (1) An IPO first-print beat is the expected outcome, so a beat alone is not unpriced; the line is more likely backlog/bookings, the Q4 implied guide and any early 2027 framework. Q3 bookings after a 3.5x Q2 driven by about $700M of modular bookings can easily come in under 1x book-to-bill, and a lumpy, concentrated order book can disappoint on that line. (2) Gross margin fell to 26.6% in H1-26 from 30.4% a year earlier, on $17.3M of negative margin on loss contracts, while new facilities ramp. Margin is a live downside line. (3) The name moves 5-7% a day on sector beta alone, and the 11-04/05 episode shows the tape can swamp company news overnight. Short interest is 12.9% of float and rising, on a 30M float, at about 13x forward EPS and $4-10 below every target. A clean beat-and-raise could move it hard, while a bookings air-pocket would meet a holder base that is already underwater. Net: modest lean up and no recommendation.
unpriced: Possibly: consensus FY26 revenue ($902M, tight range, dated 2026-10-26) implies H2 barely above H1 despite a 2.6x rise in backlog in H1. That looks like a sell-side bar inherited from the IPO model, not one revised for backlog conversion. The stock price has been driven by the sector tape, not by any revision. But a conservative IPO bar is a widely known pattern, so I cannot show it is unpriced, and the deciding line (Q3 bookings, the guide) is not visible.

recommendation.reason: Consensus arithmetic favors a revenue beat and a FY26 raise: implied H2 of $464M against H1 of $437M and backlog of $1.11B. The stock is cheap against targets and its run-in drop was sector beta. But the line a backlog story trades on is Q3 bookings and margin, and I cannot see either; after a 3.5x Q2, bookings are lumpy and margins were compressing on loss contracts. Probability is below the 65 bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 book-to-bill well under 1x, or backlog flat to down from $1.11B, or gross margin below about 25% with more loss-contract charges: any of these would make the print a downside reaction despite a revenue beat.

self_critique: A beat against a conservative IPO bar is the default expectation for first prints, so the arithmetic I lean on may already be priced, and the stock still fell 32%. The market may be pricing exactly the risks I cannot see: bookings normalising after a 3.5x Q2, margins hit by loss contracts and new-plant ramps, and doubts about customer funding after 2027. If Q3 book-to-bill is under 1x, the guide is merely reaffirmed, or margins stay in the mid-20s, a high-beta, underwater IPO with a 30M float can gap down 15% or more despite beating revenue. The overnight tape in this sector has moved 10% or more in a day, which could swamp the release.
